title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: share agents with a Microsoft Teams team
summary: Hold for corrections to governance and cost statements. Microsoft documents sharing controls beyond organisation-wide Agent Builder sharing, and the cost rationale overlooks the usage billing described in the briefing itself. The checklist also drops the sensitivity-label qualification on uploaded knowledge.

claims.claim: The July entry's first Try this step says to open the agent sharing dialog in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The Agent Builder sharing dialog accepts a name, group or email.
claims.quote: In the share dialog, enter a name, group, or email in the Add a name, group, or email box.

claims.claim: Agent Builder's sharing dialog has Can edit and Can chat access levels.
claims.quote:
The share dialog uses two access levels.
Can edit | Owner
Can chat | Chat user

claims.claim: Copilot Studio's new agent experience documents sharing with individual users, security groups or the entire organisation.
claims.quote:
For each agent, you can share with:
- Individual users by using their email or user name
- All members within security groups that you specify
- Your entire organization

claims.claim: Neither of the two cited sharing pages describes selecting a Teams team in the sharing dialog.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio share Teams team sharing dialog agent admin sharing controls' and 'Teams team Agent Builder sharing role'; opened Agent Builder share/manage and new-experience authoring-share-agent. Neither describes that picker; release notes do describe it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: This is a user-opt-in capability: users choose to share and notify, with no separate admin enablement action documented for the new option.
claims.quote: Users can search for and find teams in the agent sharing dialog box. Users can also send a notification to the main channel of that team

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Sharing controls organisation-wide Agent Builder sharing.
claims.quote: Org-wide sharing: In Agents > Settings > Sharing, control who can share agents built in Agent Builder with the organization.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply an Agent Builder sharing baseline once.
claims.quote:
POST /admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
mode | monitorMode | The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue.
An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to its note: 'Set mode to applyOnce and baseline.resources[].properties.valueObject.organizationWideSharingAssignment.userAssignmentCategory to everyone or noOne for resourceType microsoft.agent.sharing.' The properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls who can access and install agents and plugins.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.
Use User access to control how members of your organization access and install agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply an agent user-access baseline once.
claims.quote:
POST /admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to its note: 'Set mode to applyOnce and baseline.resources[].properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory to everyone or noOne for resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess.' The properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch specific to the new Teams-team share picker or its main-channel notification is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'share agents Teams team main channel notification admin switch setting Microsoft 365 Copilot'; 'Microsoft Graph Teams PowerShell agent sharing Teams team channel notification control configuration'. Read agent settings, TCM resources, sharing limits and Teams channel configuration.

claims.claim: The Sharing setting applies only to agents built with Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Sharing control only applies to agents built with Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.

claims.claim: No users disables organisation-wide sharing but still allows direct sharing with specific individuals.
claims.quote: No users - Disable sharing at the org level, but users can still share directly with specific individuals.

claims.claim: All users is the default organisation-wide Agent Builder sharing option.
claims.quote: All users (default): Everyone can share agents with the organization.

claims.claim: The admin-centre Sharing setting also offers Specific users.
claims.quote: Specific users - Restrict broad sharing permissions to designated groups.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly state that the organisation-wide Sharing setting governs the Teams-team sharing option.
claims.quote: Searched: 'share agents to Teams setting notification sharing' and 'Copilot Studio share Teams team sharing dialog agent admin sharing controls'; read agent settings and TCM sharing resource. They specify organisation-wide sharing, not this team picker.

claims.claim: The only documented agent sharing control covers organisation-wide sharing of Agent Builder agents.
claims.quote:
You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.
Only share with individuals (no security groups) ... They can't share with a security group.
claims.fix: Replace the second sentence with: 'Review the existing agent sharing settings now. Learn documents the organisation-wide Sharing control for Agent Builder agents, but does not state that this setting governs the Teams-team sharing option.' This removes the false claim that no other sharing controls are documented without asserting which Copilot Studio controls govern this picker.

claims.claim: Sharing with a team makes the agent available to that team's members.
claims.quote: share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team ... make members aware of an agent being shared with them

claims.claim: For Agent Builder, agent access and knowledge-source access are distinct, and sharing alone does not grant all source-content access.
claims.quote:
Access to an agent and access to its knowledge sources are distinct:
Sharing the agent alone doesn't grant access to all its source content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Existing file permissions and sensitivity labels apply to Agent Builder's SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge sources.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive sources: Existing file permissions and sensitivity labels apply.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Files uploaded from a device become embedded knowledge.
claims.quote: Files uploaded from a device become embedded knowledge.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, third bullet; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Uploaded files are embedded knowledge available to anyone with access to the agent.
claims.quote: Anyone who can access the agent can receive responses grounded in that content, subject to the embedded content's sensitivity-label permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: A team's main channel is a shared collaboration space rather than a named recipient list.
claims.quote:
A Teams channel is a dedicated space within a team where members can engage in conversations, share files and collaborate on projects.
In Teams, a standard channel is visible and accessible to all team members.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/standard-channels to sources for the statement about channel audience.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Groups added to Agent Builder agents can only receive Can chat, not owner access.
claims.quote: You can't add a group as an owner. When you add a group, it can only be a chat user (Can chat).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document the role assigned by the new Teams-team share picker.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Agent Builder Teams team sharing Can chat role SharePoint automatically share security groups' and 'Teams team Agent Builder sharing role'; read both sharing pages and release notes. Group roles are described, but no role is assigned to the new Teams-team picker.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Agent Builder sharing page says recipients need the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence type required by the agent's capabilities.
claims.quote: Users can only add agents that are shared with them when they have the type of Microsoft 365 Copilot license required for accessing the capabilities configured in that agent.
claims.fix: Keep this attributed to the Agent Builder page, but replace the At rollout licensing bullet with: 'Confirm recipients have the licence or billing-enabled access required for the agent's capabilities. The prerequisites page allows pay-as-you-go users to access agents without a full Copilot licence; the new Copilot Studio sharing page separately requires a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.' Both differing statements are on already cited pages: https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/prerequisites and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Using an agent without the appropriate capability licence might result in an error.
claims.quote: If a user doesn't have the appropriate license for an agent's capabilities, attempts to use the agent might result in an error.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap record names no licence.
claims.quote: With this feature, users will be able to share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team. Users can search for and find teams in the agent sharing dialog box.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page says Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is available to all Microsoft 365 users.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is a broadly accessible AI chat interface that is available to all Microsoft 365 users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: For pay-as-you-go users, tenant-data-grounded agent usage is billed in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Belong to tenants with pay-as-you-go billing enabled (consumed as Copilot Credits). Users can access Copilot Chat and agents without a full Copilot license. Usage billing applies to agents grounded in tenant data

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, with licensed and usage-billed agent access documented.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license ... Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go) ... Consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: A licence specific to the Teams-team sharing option is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'share agent Teams team licensing price Copilot Credits sharing charge' and '557947 admin license'; read prerequisites, both sharing pages and release notes. These document product/capability licences, not a separate licence for selecting a team and notifying its channel.

claims.claim: No price or meter specific to the Teams-team sharing action is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'share agent Teams team licensing price Copilot Credits sharing charge'; read prerequisites, sharing pages, release notes, and search excerpts from Billing rates and management and FAQ for Copilot Studio billing and licensing. No separate sharing-action rate was found.

claims.claim: The roadmap description discusses sharing and notification, not new agent actions.
claims.quote: share their agent with a Microsoft Teams team ... search for and find teams in the agent sharing dialog box ... send a notification to the main channel

claims.claim: Sharing is not a change to what the agent can do.
claims.quote: Searched: 'share agent Teams sharing changes capabilities actions permissions notification main channel'; read roadmap, release notes, Agent Builder sharing and Teams channel configuration. None states that the new Teams-team share operation preserves all agent capabilities.
claims.fix: Remove 'Sharing is not a change to what the agent can do.' Keep the preceding, narrower statement that the roadmap describes no new agent actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Changes to Agent Builder's Sharing setting apply only to new sharing actions.
claims.quote: Changes to the sharing setting apply only to new sharing actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Disabling organisation-wide sharing does not automatically withdraw existing access.
claims.quote:
Existing shared agents remain accessible unless you manually update their sharing settings.
These changes don't automatically revoke existing agent access permissions.

claims.claim: The Graph Tenant Configuration Management controls use preview resources in the beta API.
claims.quote: This article lists the Agent resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta. These resources also support remediation and applyOnce.

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for applyOnce.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for applying the agent configuration resources.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: The microsoft.agent.sharing resource documents everyone and noOne for organisation-wide sharing assignment.
claims.quote:
userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can share agents with everyone in the organization. | everyone, noOne
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.sharing"

claims.claim: The microsoft.agent.useraccess resource controls agent and plugin access.
claims.quote:
Controls which users or groups can use agents built by Microsoft and the organization, including plugins within agents.
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.useraccess"

claims.claim: Agent Builder documents automatic SharePoint file/folder sharing only for specific security groups.
claims.quote: Auto sharing SharePoint files and folders is only supported when sharing with specific security groups and not everyone in the organization.

claims.where: rationale: cost; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The rationale says admin and support time are the only documented costs, although the briefing documents capability-dependent licence requirements and usage billing.
claims.quote: The only documented cost is admin and support time ... usage billing (Copilot Credits) applies to agents grounded in tenant data.
claims.fix: Replace the cost rationale with: 'Low. Sharing creates admin and support work; no separate price or meter for the sharing action is published. Using the shared agent can incur Copilot Credits under pay-as-you-go, depending on its capabilities.' This distinguishes the sharing action from subsequent agent usage without inventing a sharing charge.

claims.claim: After an owner selects a team, its members are then told in the main channel that the agent exists.
claims.quote: Users can also send a notification to the main channel of that team
claims.fix: Replace 'The agent owner picks the team; the team's members are then told in the main channel that the agent exists and how to install it.' with 'The agent owner picks the team and can choose to notify its main channel that the agent exists and how to install it.'
